messages: Arya: Quick question — if we add a per-tenant rate limiter at the obsv gateway, what's the clean way to preserve billing attribution when we batch/multiplex requests? Current batching path sometimes drops per-request headers.
Miguel: We saw this in prod once — batching merges payloads and we push a synthetic envelope upstream that loses original headers. That breaks cost attribution downstream.

Arya: Right. Two immediate choices: 1) keep headers on each sub-request and carry them through the envelope, or 2) compute a merged billing key at gateway and annotate envelope level. Both have tradeoffs.
Sam: Option 1 preserves fidelity but increases envelope size a lot (n headers per batch). Also complicates shard routing since enrichers expect one billing identity per envelope.
Lee: Option 2 is smaller, simpler for enrichers, but loses per-request granularity for chargebacks when a batch contains mixed tenants (rare but happens during cross-tenant batching fallback).

Arya: For our goals (accurate unit economics + bounded envelope size) maybe we should do a hybrid: carry a primary billing key at envelope level and an optional compact per-item index that points to billing keys only when mixed-tenancy detected.

Miguel: Something like:
Envelope.metadata.billing_primary = tenant_123
Envelope.metadata.mixed_billing = true
Envelope.items[3].billing_ref = 2  # index into billing_keys[]
Envelope.metadata.billing_keys = ["tenant_123","tenant_456"]
That keeps enrichers cheap when not mixed, and gives full attribution when necessary.
Ops-bot: NOTICE: deploy-gateway v3.42 rolled out to canary (us-west) at 10:04 — watch for 5% error spike.
Sam: Implementation notes: enrichers should resolve billing_ref -> billing_keys only if mixed_billing flag true. Default path ignores item-level refs. That avoids performance regress.
Lee: Another concern — how do we handle sampling? If we pre-sample at edge and drop items, billing attribution for dropped items disappears. Should we track counts for dropped items per tenant?

Arya: Yes. Proposal: gateway emits an attribution summary per envelope when sampling occurs, e.g. `attribution_counts:{tenant_123:12,tenant_456:1}`. That way cost pipeline can still allocate sampled/tail costs robustly.
Miguel: Agree. Also need to ensure these summaries are inserted before any later dedupe or compaction so counts are stable.

Sam: Perf constraints: adding billing_keys array increases envelope size modestly. We should add a threshold where we stop embedding per-item refs and instead mark envelope as "opaque_mixed" and route to a fallthrough pipeline that keeps full per-request logs for a short retention window for audit.
Lee: Auditing pipeline is more expensive but acceptable for small % of traffic. We can cap at 0.5% of envelopes and escalate if cost rises.

Arya: Action items
- Miguel: sketch a proto change for the envelope metadata (billing_primary, mixed_billing, billing_keys, attribution_counts) — quick PR by EOD Tue
- Sam: add enrichment path guard that checks mixed_billing flag and falls back to explicit resolution only when set
- Lee: simulate envelope size impact with production p95 batch sizes and post results in thread
- Ops-bot: tag @eng-sre for canary watch on the first rollout
Sam: Also we should add unit tests for shard routing when billing_keys contains >1 entry — past bugs were subtle.
Miguel: I'll also add a compatibility flag so private deployments can opt into either 'full-per-item' or 'compact-hybrid' encoding for a few quarters.
Lee: If we get buy-in, we should do a short RFC to make the envelope schema change official. This thread can be the engineering check-in for that RFC.
Arya: Sounds good. For the RFC include: compatibility strategy, metrics to watch (envelope size p50/p95, enrich latency, attribution mismatch rate), and rollout gating criteria.
Miguel: Noted. I'll open the RFC draft and link here once PRs land.
Sam: Thanks all. Small follow-up: can we add an example consumer pseudocode for enrichers? I'll draft one.
Lee: +1 — helps oncall debug attribution issues quickly.
Arya: Closing loop — last_message_ts: 3409876599
